glosses: A place on the coast at which ships can shelter, or dock to load and unload cargo or passengers.

examples.text: peering in maps for ports and piers and roads

From the ground, Colombo's port does not look like much. Those entering it are greeted by wire fences, walls dating back to colonial times and security posts. For mariners leaving the port after lonely nights on the high seas, the delights of the B52 Night Club and Stallion Pub lie a stumble away.

glosses: A town or city containing such a place, a port city.

examples.text: More broadly, the port is seen as a litmus test for France; if its most multicultural city can foster vast Muslim enclaves viewed with broad suspicion or hostility by the police, then what hope is there elsewhere?

glosses: The left-hand side of a vessel, including aircraft, when one is facing the front. Used to unambiguously refer to directions relative to the vessel structure, rather than to a person or object on board.
A sweep rower that primarily rows with an oar on the port side.

examples.text: Each eight has four ports and four starboards.

glosses: Of or relating to port, the left-hand side of a vessel when facing the bow.

examples.text: on the port side

glosses: To turn or put to the left or larboard side of a ship; said of the helm.

examples.text: Port your helm!

glosses: To dock at a port.

examples.text: The tall ships will port in Pugwash during its annual Harbourfest Celebrations[…]
We have to wait until the ship ports, buddy, and then we can get you the help you need.
Our cruise ship ported at Mykonos, a small island off the coast of Greece, for an overnight stay.
